finding.claim: POST /profile/avatar makes a server-side GET to an attacker-supplied URL. The only check is a string prefix 'https://', and axios follows redirects by default, so the request can be redirected to http:// or internal hosts (e.g. 169.254.169.254, users.internal:8080). Only the response byte length is returned (blind SSRF with a length oracle).
finding.source: server.js:10 - req.body.avatarUrl from the JSON body of POST /profile/avatar (express.json at server.js:5); no authentication in this file
finding.sink: server.js:14 - axios.get(url, {responseType:'arraybuffer'}) with default redirect following; no maxRedirects, timeout, or maxContentLength

trace.note: outbound GET; axios follows 3xx Location headers, including switching to http://, so the scheme check does not apply to redirect targets

finding.guards_checked: server.js:11 scheme-prefix check only: no URL parsing, no hostname/IP denylist or allowlist, no DNS-resolution check, no redirect restriction (maxRedirects not set to 0), no response size or timeout limits. Direct https:// URLs to internal hosts with trusted certificates are also not blocked. Route has no auth in this file. Versions of axios/Express are unknown (no package.json or lockfile); redirect-following is based on axios's documented default, not verified by running code.

verdict.guard_found: none. The only check is server.js:11, which tests typeof === "string" and startsWith("https://"). Nothing parses the hostname or restricts IPs, and axios.get at server.js:14 sets no maxRedirects, timeout, or maxContentLength. The route has no auth middleware (server.js:5 is only express.json).
verdict.reason: server.js:10 reads req.body.avatarUrl from an unauthenticated POST /profile/avatar, server.js:11 is a prefix-only check, and server.js:14 issues a server-side axios.get that follows redirects by default, so the request can reach internal hosts or http:// targets; only the byte length is returned at server.js:15, which makes this a blind SSRF with a length oracle. The redirect-following behavior relies on axios's documented default and was not verified by running code, but the finding holds regardless because direct https:// URLs to internal hosts are also unblocked.
